claim_text: Peptide-level analysis of PXD036678 iTRAQ-LC-CE-iBAQ-peptides.txt (29,841 peptide rows, 21.7 MB) confirms the protein-level finding from v1.2: only prkci (UniProt Q90XF2, 6 unique peptide sequences including DMCSMDNDQLFTMK, ELVNDDEDIDWVQTEK, KLPEEHAR) and vangl2 (UniProt Q8UVJ6, 3 unique peptide sequences including ELEDSSPLECR, LQDDEAAASPK, SVTIQAPGEPLLDAESTR) are detected from the 14-candidate minimal set. The other 12 candidates (osr1, pax2a, lhx1a, wt1a, mafba, cdh17, myh9a, pard3, podxl, itga1, itgb1a, sept7b) are absent. Sanity check on the dataset's FASTA database confirms 10,747 unique protein accessions across all peptide rows — the absence is NOT a database-mismatch artifact. The 12-candidate absence is biologically consistent with developmental timing: TFs and effectors specific to pronephros are not expected to be expressed at protein level at 2-5.3 hpf (pre-W1; pronephros specification begins at W2 = 10 hpf).
framework_applied: Self-Discover (Tier 2) — per reasoning-frameworks-catalog.md §Tier 2. Sub-module M11 (FASTA-database sanity check) added in v1.3 to distinguish biological absence from DB-mismatch.
expected_outcome_if_h1: The same peptide-level analysis applied to a W2-W4 zebrafish proteome (Wan JPR 2023 or BioRxiv 2026 once PXD is obtained) will detect at least 9 of the 12 currently-absent candidates with multi-peptide evidence. Specifically: pax2a, lhx1a, wt1a detected at W2 onset (10 hpf), cdh17 at W3 (14 hpf), mafba/podxl/sept7b at W4 (18-24 hpf), itga1/itgb1a at sustained W4.
expected_outcome_if_h0: If a W2-W4 proteome detects fewer than 6 of the 12 currently-absent candidates, this would suggest: (a) significant transcript-protein discordance for kidney TFs (transcripts detectable but protein below MS detection limits even in mature tissue), or (b) the candidate set is incomplete or contains incorrect entries that need revision. Notable alternative: pax2a/wt1a may have very low protein abundance even at peak expression (TFs are notoriously hard to detect by shotgun MS).
observable_at: Access to any zebrafish 10-24 hpf proteome with peptide-level data (Wan JPR 2023, BioRxiv 2026.03.24, or future deposit). Falsifiable by direct re-running this peptide-level scan on a W2-W4 protein table.
